title: Complexe de De Rham à puissance divisée [conférence de 1976 à l’IHÉS] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: notes for the 1976 IHES talk on the divided-power (PD) de Rham complex. Grothendieck works with a completed 'k-algèbre différentielle à 2 simpliciale' (probably a bi-(co)simplicial differential graded algebra), written Â_{k*}. Its building blocks are completed divided-power series rings. Ŝ_k ≅ k{{T}} is the completed PD polynomial algebra in one variable. In the next degree there is Ŝ_k{{X_0}} ≅ k{{T}}{{X_0}} ≅ k{{X_0,X_1}}, where X^{(n)} denotes divided powers.

An endomorphism φ_* of this structure is determined by finitely many data: series A, B_i (i≥1) in Ŝ_k{{X_0}}, the images of the generators. Together with these comes the degree-0 component φ_0, determined by φ_0(T) = Σ_{j≥1} λ_j T^{(j)}. This has no constant term, so substitution into PD series makes sense (T lies in the PD ideal).

Write A = Σ_{j≥1} a_j X_0^{(j)}, with a_j = Σ_h a_{j,h} T^{(h)}. Equivalently A = Σ_{i≥1, j≥0} α_{ij} X_0^{(i)} X_1^{(j)}. Compatibility of φ_* with the simplicial/differential structure (face maps or the differential relating X_0, X_1 and T) forces the linear coefficients to agree: a_{1,0} = α_{1,0} = λ_1.

This scalar is named (after crossing out 'discriminant' and 'indicateur') the 'déterminant' Δ(φ_*). It also makes sense for a morphism Â_k → Â_{k'} lying over a ring map k → k', in which case Δ lies in k'.

Theorem:
- φ_* is an automorphism iff Δ(φ_*) ∈ k^×.
- Δ is multiplicative under composition and Δ(1) = 1.
- Hence Δ is a character of the group Ω(k) = Aut(Â_{k*}) to G_m(k).

In modern terms, this is the inverse function theorem for PD formal power series in one variable: a substitution T ↦ λ_1 T + higher terms is invertible iff λ_1 is a unit. The multiplicativity is the chain rule for linear terms. The purpose is apparently to study the automorphism group Ω(k) of the PD de Rham model, viewed as a group-valued functor of k, and to produce its basic character Δ.
errors: Terminology is inconsistent: the definition renames the invariant 'déterminant' (crossing out 'discriminant' and 'indicateur'), but the theorem still says 'indicateur'.
No proof is given. 'Un calcul immédiat' hides that the identity a_{1,0}=α_{1,0}=λ_1 depends on the precise face/differential maps of the bi-simplicial structure, which are not written on this page.

Sufficiency (Δ invertible ⇒ φ_* invertible) needs more than the formal inverse function theorem for φ_0: the higher components (A, B_i) must also be shown to be invertible. Presumably they are recursively determined, but this is not argued here.
Ω(k) is defined as an automorphism group of the 'k-alg diff à 2 simpl', yet the precise structure (bisimplicial vs cosimplicial, completed in which topology) is left implicit.

ideas.what: Endomorphisms of the completed PD de Rham bi-simplicial algebra are determined by PD series data; their linear coefficient λ_1 is an invariant.
ideas.modern_name: linear term / Jacobian of an automorphism of the PD formal line (formal inverse function theorem for divided power series)
ideas.usually_credited_to: folklore (formal groups / PD calculus; Berthelot, Illusie for PD de Rham)

ideas.what: Criterion: φ_* is an automorphism iff Δ(φ_*) is a unit; Δ gives a homomorphism Ω(k) → G_m(k).
ideas.modern_name: character det: Aut(PD formal line model) → G_m
ideas.where_published: possibly in the unpublished 1976 IHES talk material only

ideas.what: Introducing the group functor Ω(k) = Aut of the PD de Rham (bi)simplicial algebra as an object of study.
ideas.modern_name: automorphism group of a (PD) dg/cosimplicial model; related to symmetries of crystalline/PD de Rham models

missed.claim: Grothendieck defines a group functor Ω(k) of automorphisms of the completed PD de Rham bi-simplicial algebra and its character Δ to G_m. On this page the study of Ω (its kernel, structure as a pro-unipotent extension, etc.) is only begun.
missed.quote: donc Δ est un homom. du groupe Ω(k) = Aut_{k-alg diff à 2 simpl}(Â_{k*}) dans k* = G_m(k)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: The symmetries of PD/crystalline de Rham models are relevant to recent work on derived de Rham and prismatic cohomology and on functorial models of the PD de Rham complex. Whether Grothendieck computed Ω more fully elsewhere in this file would need checking. On this page alone it is routine.

deep.surprise_reason: The content is a routine inverse function theorem and Jacobian character for divided-power series. The only mildly notable point is the explicit introduction of the automorphism group Ω(k) of the PD de Rham model, which is unpublished but not evidently deep from this page.
transcription_corrections: Line 3 reads 'à 2 simplic. Â_{k*}, ayant[?]/donné[?] :' — 'à noyau' seems unlikely; it introduces the data A, B_i.
In the definition, the crossed-out words are 'discriminant' (and 'indicateur'), with 'déterminant' written above, plus the insertion 'noté Δ(φ_*)'.
In the parenthesis of the 'Posons' line, read 'a_j ∈ Ŝ_k ≃ k{{T}}, j≥0' as in the image (the j≥1/j≥0 indexing is inconsistent in the original).
'Ceci posé' is likely, since the image shows an abbreviated word before 'un calcul immédiat montre'.
Page number 175 is written at the bottom left.
